findings.claim: cmdAdvance picked its out-of-lock runs (the done gate's GREEN re-run and the verified battery) from unlocked snapshots, then judged a possibly different record inside the lock. A pin recorded while the gate ran reached done without being re-run, and handoff called it GREEN. A concurrent phase advance skipped the run entirely.
findings.proof: Run advance X done with a pin that sleeps, and meanwhile run red-check X --command "echo 'x FAILED'; exit 1" to record a new pin mid-run. The lock judged the new record against the old greenFailures, reached done, and printed 'pin GREEN at done' for a command that still exits 1. The fix takes ONE snapshot that chooses every run. refuseMovedRecord (tools/task-state.mjs:1019) then refuses inside the lock when the events differ from that snapshot, which also closes the phase race. The self-test case 'advance done refuses a record that moved while the gate ran its pins' (selfTestCliRace) makes the race deterministic.

findings.claim: loadOwnedFindings told the operator to restore a register from git, which drops every finding since the last commit. The round-1 shared findingsRepair still printed 'rm <register> && prepare' after EVERY failed read, including conflict-marked or invalid registers that hold findings. That is the destructive re-mint adversarial#17 forbids.

Pins were retired by command string alone, ignoring event order. Re-pinning a once-retired command recorded a dead pin while red-check reported success. One pin-retire also dropped every sibling pin sharing the command, whatever its --expect. retiredPins is now order-aware (a retirement reaches back only), and pin-retire takes --expect to retire that one pin and prints the count it retired.

runLawRepairCases is not named selfTest*, so it leaked its fixture riskClass 'docs-only' into reader-existence's production corpus. That made the accepted RISK_CLASSES.docs-only NO_PRODUCER row read as stale, so reader-existence failed at b5c1d3b.

The certified commit b5c1d3b, and every commit through c004bb9, fails the selftest battery when checked out alone (reader-existence). Nothing runs the battery per commit. The seq-14 verified transition judged a later combined working tree, not b5c1d3b.
findings.justification: History cannot be rewritten. HEAD has been battery-green since 26c1584 (b9523a6's cut, then 26c1584 accepted the SEVERITIES rows). Register note, as the verifier asked: the seq-14 `verified` transition (2026-09-27T08:02:22Z) ran `npm run selftest` on a working tree that already carried b9523a6 and 26c1584, so it certifies the combined sweep, not b5c1d3b. b5c1d3b..c004bb9 are each red alone. Closing the per-commit gap is a CI/hook policy change outside this task's two files. The cheap pre-commit cure is not requested because the hook judges the working tree, not the staged tree. In a shared tree it would refuse one author's commit over another's unstaged edits: in this session the live gate-registry was red on another group's in-flight file. The sound cure is CI running the battery on each commit of the pushed range, alongside the task-commit binding work (issue #8).

findings.claim: Status judged the register named by the record's body id, while advance and handoff used the file's id, and parseTaskRecord never tied the two together. A copied record read 'unblocked' where advance refused, and the status listing showed it twice. findingsPath and metricRow also joined an unvalidated id into a path.

terminalAdvanceRefusal could not be reached from the CLI because mutateTask's seam refuses terminal records first. Its bespoke 'reopened as a NEW task' text was never printed, yet a self-test case pinned it. evaluateTransition now uses terminalAppendRefusal (the seam's own words), and the dead function is deleted.

At b5c1d3b, the comments on FENCE_SURFACE, TASK_ID, findingsPath and decisionHeadingExists said sibling tools derive from them, but no sibling imported them, and the three fence-surface copies disagreed.

The CLI battery case's fixture script spelled 'x FAILED' literally, and npm echoes a script's source as its banner. The refusal therefore carried the token even when the run never printed it. The fixture now assembles the token at run time on stderr.

The header claimed the --self-test drives every refusal. Round 1's rewrite still said 'the CLI-only laws' while pin-retire's matching and already-retired laws, scope's repetition law and new's duplicate id went undriven.

pinlessDoneRefusal's alternative remedy, '(or pin a check that still fails: red-check …)', could never clear it. The done gate re-runs the pin GREEN, so a check that fails now lands in the green-failure refusal, whose retire remedy loops back. The remedy now names the real RED→GREEN arc: pin against the PRE-fix source, then restore the fix.

handoffReport called obligations() without the resolveEvidenceMissing fact its caller computed. At adversarial with vanished resolve evidence, the handoff printed the unblocked 'done will re-run N pin(s)' line where advance refuses. The fact is now forwarded.
red-check's pin-expect cutover refusal, moved ahead of runPinCommand, had no case. Deleting it, or moving it back below the run, left both self-tests green.
Two repaired branches had no discriminating case: pinlessDoneRefusal's NON_CODE allowance (a pinless docs-only task reaching done) and adoptionRefusal's done half (adopt-chain's only terminal guard).

Commands that run arbitrary shell before appending judged only the terminal law first. mutateTask's chain-integrity refusal fired after the run, so red-check on a tampered chained record ran its pin, and advance ran the whole selftest battery (or every done-gate pin twice), before refusing.

The terminal law holds only at task-state's writer. adversarial-runner's prepare, record, resolve and wont-fix still rewrite a done task's findings register: prepare re-mints passStartedAt and sweptBase/sweptHead, and record adds UNRESOLVED findings. status still reads 'done', so 'register aggregates clean' no longer holds.
